description:
Found by the HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9, docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy.md, point 8). Counting bytes (a 256-bin histogram, per window or over a whole binary, then Shannon entropy) is a common job with no catalog entry and no docs/performance.md entry, so building a fair optimised Elixir baseline meant guessing (:counters, 8 bytes per binary-pattern step from performance.md 2.2/2.3, results appended to a binary per 2.1). The cold tester's own numbers (in the log, loaded machine, not a catalog measurement): first pass bin_to_list |> Enum.frequencies 9 MB/s; :counters + 8-byte steps 138 MB/s; kernel ~2250 MB/s (16x, one process vs one call, not split over schedulers).

Done when examples/ has a byte-histogram (and windowed-entropy) example in the usual shape (Defk.Bench.report, expected verdict declared before the numbers, realistic size declared), the Elixir side tries at least Enum.frequencies, :counters/:atomics, a tuple of counts, binary-pattern steps of 1 and 8 bytes and a split over all schedulers, the kernel is compared one process vs one call and over all schedulers, and docs/performance.md gets an entry (section 2, 'counting bytes') with numbers, conditions and status; measuring.md's pointer to '2.12 Dense counters' is updated to the new entry if it is the better one.

comments.text: Done on branch defk-9p6.28/byte-histogram (commits c177321, 15e6642): examples/byte_histogram.exs, two DEFK_RESULT lines (byte_histogram, windowed_entropy), both expected and measured good, baseline optimised. PROVISIONAL, under load (load 12-31, seven runs). Realistic size 16 MB (half random, half text), 4 KiB windows. Histogram parallel vs parallel (12 chunks each, Task.async per chunk): Elixir 8.7-10.9 ms vs defk 1.40-1.71 ms = 5.5-6.6x; one process vs one call 11.4-12.7x (43-47 vs 3.6-3.8 ms, 0.39 vs 4.6 GB/s); sweep 4 KB 24-28x, 64 KB 19-23x, 1 MB 17.7-19.4x. Entropy parallel vs parallel 12.5-18.6 vs 1.83-2.0 ms = 6.7-10.2x; one process vs one call 82-89 vs 4.7-5.2 ms = 17.0-17.9x. Elixir variants at 16 MB, ms: Enum.frequencies ~2200-2700 (136-169 at 1 MB), Map.update ~3300, 256-tuple setelement ~1000-1300, :binary.matches per value ~400, :counters 1B 112-115, :counters 8B 101-103, :counters comprehension 116-123, :atomics 1B 91-92, :atomics 8B 75-77, 16-bit pairs into a 65,536-slot :atomics 43-44 (best; E9 wins below 512 KB, the baseline is the hybrid), in 12 chunks: :counters 8B 16-18, shared write_concurrency :counters 23-26, :atomics 8B 12-13, pairs 8.7-9.9 (baseline). Entropy: :counters get+put 121-123, :atomics exchange 90-91, + term table 84 (one process), 12 chunks 13.4-14.4 (baseline). Kernel: four interleaved tables 1.6x over one table; window bounds written max/min to drop per-byte bounds checks (7.0 -> 4.7 ms). Correctness: histograms exact, entropies bit for bit (log2 on both sides since defk-ngj landed mid-ticket; same order, term table on both sides), native vs Elixir mode on edge cases and odd windows, forced yields on 1 MB, w = 0 raises in both modes. Docs: examples/README.md row (Where defk helps), performance.md 2.16 'Counting bytes' (runnable sketch), 6.18 'Counting into a table' (after main's 6.16/6.17), a pointer from 2.12 to 2.16, measuring.md now points counting bytes at 2.16 and keys at 2.12.

title: Catalog: byte histogram and windowed entropy, with optimised Elixir baselines
